tasks.title: Add Signup page with shared in-memory credential store
tasks.description:
1. WHAT: Introduce a shared in-memory credential store, a new Signup component, and wire both into the existing Login + App flow so that users who sign up have their credentials appended to the live store and can subsequently log in.

2. READ FIRST: Read src/components/Login.tsx (current hardcoded auth logic), src/App.tsx (auth routing), src/components/Login.css (styles to reuse), src/components/Login.test.tsx (test patterns to follow).

3. FILES:
   - CREATE src/auth/credentialStore.ts — a module that holds an in-memory array of {email, password} objects pre-seeded with {email: 'test@gmail.com', password: 'test123'}. Export two functions: `validateCredentials(email, password): boolean` and `addCredential(email, password): void`.
   - MODIFY src/components/Login.tsx — remove the two module-level constants (VALID_EMAIL, VALID_PASSWORD) and replace the hardcoded check with a call to `validateCredentials` from the new store. Pass no new props; the store is a singleton.
   - CREATE src/components/Signup.tsx — a functional component accepting `{ onSignup: () => void, onGoToLogin: () => void }`. It renders a form with email, password, and confirm-password fields. On submit: validate that passwords match (show inline error if not), check that email is not already registered via a new exported `emailExists(email): boolean` helper in the store (show error if duplicate), then call `addCredential` and invoke `onSignup`. Follow the exact JSX/class-name structure of Login.tsx.
   - ADD `emailExists(email): boolean` export to src/auth/credentialStore.ts.
   - MODIFY src/App.tsx — add a `view` state: `'login' | 'signup'`. When `isAuthenticated` is false and `view === 'login'` render `<Login onLogin={handleLogin} onGoToSignup={() => setView('signup')} />`. When `view === 'signup'` render `<Signup onSignup={handleLogin} onGoToLogin={() => setView('login')} />`. Update the LoginProps interface in Login.tsx to include `onGoToSignup: () => void` and render a 'Sign up' link/button below the submit button.
   - MODIFY src/components/Login.css — add a `.login-link` style (text button, no border/background, colored link appearance) for the sign-up link.
   - CREATE src/components/Signup.test.tsx — tests covering: form renders email/password/confirm-password fields and submit button; mismatched passwords shows inline error and does not call onSignup; duplicate email shows inline error and does not call onSignup; valid unique email + matching passwords calls onSignup once; 'Back to login' link calls onGoToLogin. Follow the describe/it pattern in Login.test.tsx using @testing-library/react and userEvent.
   - CREATE src/auth/credentialStore.test.ts — tests covering: validateCredentials returns true for seed credentials; returns false for unknown email; addCredential adds a new user that then validates successfully; emailExists returns true for existing email and false for new one. Note: because the store is a module-level singleton, reset or re-import between tests using vi.resetModules() as needed, or structure tests so they do not conflict.

4. APPROACH: The credential store is a plain TypeScript module (no React context needed) — a module-level `let users: Array<{email: string; password: string}>` array. This keeps the diff minimal. Reuse Login.css class names in Signup (same card/form/field/label/input/error/submit selectors) — no separate Signup.css needed.

5. PATTERNS: Mirror Login.tsx structure exactly for Signup.tsx. Mirror Login.test.tsx patterns for Signup.test.tsx.
acceptance_criteria: The app shows a 'Sign In' form by default when the page loads
A 'Sign up' link or button is visible on the login page and clicking it navigates to a signup form
The signup form has email, password, and confirm password fields plus a submit button
Submitting the signup form with mismatched passwords shows an inline error message on screen
After successfully signing up with a new email and matching passwords the user is logged in and the calculator is visible
After signing up, logging out and logging back in with the newly created credentials succeeds (calculator appears)

tasks.title: Run full test suite to validate signup feature
tasks.description:
Run the complete Vitest test suite to confirm all tests pass after the signup feature is added. Execute the following commands:
1. npx vitest run src/auth/credentialStore.test.ts
2. npx vitest run src/components/Signup.test.tsx
3. npx vitest run src/components/Login.test.tsx
4. npx vitest run (full suite)
5. npx tsc --noEmit
All must exit with code 0.
acceptance_criteria: npx vitest run src/auth/credentialStore.test.ts exits code 0 with all tests passing
npx vitest run src/components/Signup.test.tsx exits code 0 with at least 5 tests passing
npx vitest run src/components/Login.test.tsx exits code 0 with all existing tests passing
npx vitest run exits code 0 — full suite green
npx tsc --noEmit exits code 0 — no TypeScript errors
